HAND SCALE / Branches of arts already present

Tarot, Lenormand, Sibilla & playing-card systems.

Different card-reading families whose decks, layouts and interpretive conventions should be identified separately.

LEXICON / LANGUAGE & MEANING

Names in context.

Tarot
Tarot

A card family with trumps and suited cards, used for games and in distinct divinatory traditions.

Lenormand
Lenormand

A family of oracle decks and reading systems, especially the 36-card Petit Lenormand.

Sibilla
Sibilla

A name used for several illustrated oracle-card traditions; identify the particular edition.

Playing-card reading
Lectura de naipes

Divinatory use of a named ordinary playing-card deck.

Cartomancy
Cartomancia

An umbrella term for divination using cards.

PROVENANCE & INTERPRETATION

A practice,
a setting.

European playing cards and tarot have documented histories of play and later divinatory use. Lenormand and Sibilla decks have distinct imagery and reading traditions; matching card counts alone does not make decks equivalent.

FIELD NOTE / METHOD

Keep a record.

  1. Name the deck, edition, card count and reading system.
  2. Record the question, layout and draw order before interpreting.
  3. Photograph the whole spread and read with the chosen deck’s conventions.
POTPOURRI / PHOTO GUIDE

What to include.

  • Use an overhead view with every card readable and no cropped positions.
  • Mark the first card, orientation and draw order; add a close image for small card text.
